what_happened: The job "Open the early pull request right after the candidate commit" (20261025-110525-8hzb) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic judged that the reading misread the request. The reading assumed Athena's checks run before the early pull request call. In the code they run after it: the candidate commit is made, then admission and fingerprinting run, then early_pr is called (run.rs:1645), and the routed checks start at about line 1700. So moving the call ahead of admission saves seconds, not the 12 minutes the request blames. The critic named two likely real causes the reading never traced. Baseline checks run on the base commit before the producer. Landing replaces the early head with a different landing commit (replace_early), so CI runs fresh on the landing SHA. It raised two major findings: the planned move does not change when CI starts relative to Athena's checks, and the criterion 1 test uses the "candidate …" UI line as its boundary, which does not show the call happens before the checks. It also raised two minor findings: pushing before admission sends refused candidates (personal data, size) to the remote, and the admission-refusal never-merged test depends on that risky ordering. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The request named a fix (move the call earlier) and a timing figure, but nothing required the reading or planner to check that figure against the real stage order and durations before planning around it. The class already exists for a speed request whose trigger point was chosen without the measured timeline. Here the code already showed the early call precedes the checks, but the reading took the request's premise as true. The reading step has no rule to confirm a request's causal claim in the code. The critic is the first stage to trace the code, so the gap surfaces only after the planning rounds are spent. The three-round cap keeps no partial result, and a retry starts without the critic's findings. Demonstrations were also built on a proxy boundary (a UI line) and not on the event that matters (the checks starting).
prevention: For any request that claims a delay or speed-up, the reading stage must first produce a timeline from the code and the recorded run timings: each stage in order, its measured duration, and where the claimed delay sits. The reading must state the cause from that timeline, and must stop and flag the premise if the code contradicts it. Tests for ordering must observe the real event (CI start versus checks start), not a nearby log line. The critic's findings and the timeline must carry into a retry. This would stop the whole class: speed changes planned on a premise nobody checked against measured stage order.
proposed_request: Find out why CI for a job's early pull request finishes late relative to Athena's own checks, and fix the cause. Start from a measured timeline of one recent job, taken from its recorded run data: candidate commit, admission, fingerprinting, the early pull request call, baseline checks on the base commit, producer, routed checks, landing, and CI start and end. Note that the early_pr call already happens before the routed checks (run.rs, produce_and_verify), so do not just move it. Check these two leads and any others the timeline shows: (1) landing replaces the early head with a different landing commit (replace_early), so CI reruns on a new SHA; (2) the early CI run has not finished when landing begins. Fix the cause where it starts, or if it lies outside this change, say so and name it. Acceptance: (a) a short written timeline with measured durations that shows where the delay comes from; (b) a test that observes when CI is triggered relative to the start of the routed checks, not a UI line; (c) after the change, a landing that follows a green early CI run reuses that result and does not start a new full CI run on the landing commit, shown by a test with a fake host; (d) candidates refused by admission (personal data, size) are never pushed to the remote; (e) cargo test and the repo checks pass.
